speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to help me understand your condition, could you please describe exactly how the spinning sensation feels and if it is triggered by head movements? Additionally, have you experienced any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or nausea alongside this symptom?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The brief duration of your spinning sensation (3 minutes), the sudden onset while lying down, and your immediate return to baseline are classic signs of BPPV. Since you have no hearing loss or neurological deficits, I do not need further tests at this time; we can proceed with a bedside exam to confirm the diagnosis.
